The Mark IX departs from its landing craft relatives most fundamentally in propulsion. Two engine nacelles replace the single nacelle of the Mark VII, providing a safe thrust of 7 and maximum thrust of 11, giving the craft genuine interceptor performance against aerospace fighters. Weighing 200 tons, the Mark IX carries more than double the mass of the Mark VII, with the additional tonnage distributed across a heavier weapons suite, expanded fuel capacity, and substantially more armor.

Armament centers on a forward nose battery of a Large Pulse Laser and an ER Large Laser, suited to extended engagement ranges in deep space. Four medium pulse lasers in the wings provide close-range firepower once the craft closes. Fifteen freezer-model heat sinks manage the energy load. A Beagle active probe allows the Mark IX to support friendly fighters by disrupting hostile ECM fields, a capability that proved decisive in the heavily contested electronic warfare environments of the Jihad. Twenty-seven tons of standard armor protect the hull, concentrated at the nose. The craft carries only three tons of cargo, reflecting its exclusively combat-oriented mission. The dual-nacelle propulsion system is the Mark IX's most visually distinctive feature, making it immediately recognizable alongside the single-nacelle landing craft variants.

The Ares Attack Craft Mark IX is a deep space escort vessel that emerged from the Jihad, representing a radical departure from the landing craft heritage of its name. Produced by Federated Boeing, the Mark IX was developed as large-scale naval operations expanded during the Jihad and the renewed growth of Inner Sphere WarShip fleets created demand for capable close-escort small craft. The design shares the hull dimensions of the Mark VII family but replaces the single engine nacelle with a dual-nacelle propulsion system that nearly doubles available thrust, and trades the landing craft's cargo utility for a heavily armored, deeply armed combat platform. Introduced in 3077 and proven during the campaign for Terra, the Mark IX subsequently attracted license production from Lyran, Republic, and Draconis Combine manufacturers, extending the Ares lineage into the modern era of Inner Sphere naval warfare.

The Mark IX is deployed exclusively in naval escort and deep space defense roles, assigned to WarShip flotillas and large DropShip formations rather than ground assault wings. Federated Suns naval forces were the first to integrate it, fitting Mark IXs into Arondight-class WarShip complements during the Jihad. Its dual nacelles and high thrust give it genuine interceptor capability, and the Beagle active probe makes it particularly effective in ECM-heavy environments. Licensed production spread the design to Lyran, Republic, and Combine fleets in the post-Jihad era, and all four major naval powers continue to operate it into the ilClan period. The Mark IX is rarely encountered in planetary assault roles, its three-ton cargo bay making it unsuitable for the transport missions that define the rest of the Ares family.

The Mark IX traces its origins to the Mk.III Assault Craft of 2451, the dedicated fighter-engagement branch of the original Ares family. IncStar Dynamics built the three-branch family on a single common hull: the Mk.I as the long-range landing craft, the Mk.II as the close attack landing craft, and the Mk.III as the assault craft. All three operated together in HAF wings through the Age of War and into the Star League period before the family was gradually replaced by lighter successor frames from 2476 onward.

The Star League's collapse ended the Ares lineage in its original form. IncStar Dynamics dissolved during the First Succession War after dropping the Ares name as the collapse of the Ares Conventions made the designation politically awkward. The long-range landing craft branch survived in the form of the Mark VII, which entered production by 2824 and spread across the Inner Sphere under multiple manufacturers. The close attack landing craft branch had no direct successor. The assault craft branch went entirely dormant, with no active production line carrying the Mk.III's fighter-engagement mission forward.

Universal Air maintained the Ares design archives through the Succession Wars and the Clan Invasion era. The Zhen Niao, whose name translates roughly as "Poisonfeather Bird," is a Small Craft designed and produced by Rashpur-Owens Incorporated on Capella for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. Introduced in 3101, it was conceived not as a conventional combat vessel but as an armed noncombatant, a platform for electronic warfare and orbital reconnaissance capable of operating without fighter escort. The CCAF adopted it rapidly, recognizing its value as an intelligence asset that could fly random powered orbits, blend into civilian intrasystem traffic, and deny enemy aerospace forces the predictable patterns they relied on to hunt satellite-class craft. Understated in appearance and deceptive in purpose, the Zhen Niao represents the Confederation's preference for asymmetric capabilities over brute-force aerospace superiority.

The Zhen Niao serves in CCAF aerospace screening and electronic warfare assignments, deployed in pairs from dedicated Capellan DropShips to maintain mutual support during extended independent operations. Its orbital profile mimics civilian intrasystem traffic, and crews are trained to maintain patterns consistent with commercial vessels. The craft's fuel capacity supports lengthy missions without tender contact, making it well suited for advance reconnaissance assignments ahead of conventional operations.

Commands tasked with planetary assault or large-scale interdiction benefit most from the Zhen Niao. Its limited armament makes direct engagement inadvisable, and commanders who treat it as a combat asset rather than a reconnaissance platform misuse it. Used correctly, it provides actionable intelligence at a cost and risk profile well below that of a dedicated aerospace fighter screen.

Rashpur-Owens Incorporated developed the Zhen Niao in the years following the Jihad, responding to CCAF requirements for a dedicated electronic warfare and orbital reconnaissance platform that could operate without an escort footprint. The design entered service in 3101, marking an expansion of Rashpur-Owens' traditional focus on large aerospace vessels into the Small Craft category. The Capellan Confederation integrated the type into DropShip operations quickly, typically deploying pairs of craft on intelligence-gathering missions ahead of conventional forces.

The Warrior House Offensive of 3112 provided the Zhen Niao's first significant operational test. Two craft deployed from a Capellan DropShip to make competing orbital passes over Republic-held worlds, gathering first-scan intelligence on planetary defenses and troop dispositions before the assault began. Davion aerospace fighters rose to intercept them. The two Zhen Niaos used their electronic systems and fuel reserves to run, laying minefields and counting on their ECM to protect them. Only one escaped. The surviving craft's data, however, proved critical to the offensive's initial success, and the engagement was studied afterward as a demonstration of both the type's value and its vulnerability when denied the element of surprise.

Later operations at Tikonov revealed a different dimension of the craft's capability. Operating covertly from Capellan merchant DropShips over an extended period, Zhen Niao crews gathered detailed intelligence on a succession of Republic worlds prior to formal military operations. RAF analysts determined after the fact that the craft had maintained orbit for nearly a week at a stretch, refueling at Capellan merchants in transit, before Confederation ground forces moved. The intelligence contributed materially to the depth of the Capellan advance through Republic lines.

By the Dark Age, the Zhen Niao had earned a quiet reputation within the CCAF as one of the more effective surveillance platforms in the Confederation's aerospace inventory, prized by commanders who understood how to use it and largely invisible to those who did not.

The NL-45 Gunboat is a combat picket small craft built by the United Outworlders Corporation at their Ramora factory for the Raven Alliance. Introduced in 3094, the NL-45 continues the tradition of NL-series military transports begun during the Star League era. Designed to fill a role that the corporation's civilian craft could not, the Gunboat serves as a patrol and light escort vessel for Clan naval assets. Since its debut the NL-45 has proven a valuable export product, becoming the default platform for any Clan needing a small craft to patrol near space, deploy boarding parties to armed vessels, or screen larger formations during orbital operations.

The base NL-45 is the sole production configuration of the Gunboat. Its combination of enhanced electronic warfare systems, battle armor transport capability, and orbital drop support makes it well suited to the Raven Alliance's doctrine of leveraging naval superiority through distributed small craft screens and rapid boarding actions against both military and pirate targets.

The NL-45 was developed by the United Outworlders Corporation to meet a specific gap in the Raven Alliance's naval order of battle. While the Alliance possessed significant WarShip and DropShip assets inherited from Clan Snow Raven's long tradition of naval excellence, it lacked a purpose-built small craft for the picket and boarding roles that its growing territorial responsibilities demanded. UOC, a Periphery manufacturer with limited military production experience, adapted existing civilian small craft expertise to produce the Gunboat, filling a niche that more established Clan manufacturers had neglected.

The NL-45 saw its first major combat deployment during the Raven Alliance's invasion of Kirbyville. Beta Galaxy used the Gunboats extensively to secure the system, dispatching them to nearly every manned satellite in orbit. Resistance was met with autocannon fire directed at life support systems, quickly discouraging further opposition. When the Third Periphery Guard committed to atmospheric entry, the Gunboats shifted to an aerospace screening role, exploiting their ECM suites to offset the numerical advantage held by defending fighters. A second wave of NL-45s then accompanied Arcadia-class DropShips to deliver battle armor directly into the capital while the Arcadias engaged ground targets.

The Gunboat has also featured prominently in Lyran operations against the Jade Falcon Golden Ordun. Falcon WarShips routinely deployed NL-45s as defensive screens, leveraging the craft's ECM capabilities to complicate attacks by Lyran aerospace units. During the Lyran assault on Wroclaw, NL-45s formed part of the defensive barrier that forced attackers into close range where the Falcon fleet's heavier armament dominated. The craft's most notable defensive action occurred at Timkovichi, where a pair of NL-45s generated an electronics screen that spoofed three of five nuclear weapons launched at the WarShip White Aerie. The heart of the Würger is the Lockheed/CBM Progeny II tactical computer. This system unifies the craft's offensive and defensive electronics under a single management framework, and also integrates the cooling system and engine control. The Progeny II takes hundreds of sensor readings per second from myriad onboard sensors, making continuous synergistic adjustments to maximize the effectiveness of each installed system. This allows the Würger to respond rapidly to changing battlefield conditions without relying on pilot interpretation alone.

As a small craft optimized for orbital interdiction and point-defense screening, the Würger trades the raw firepower of heavier aerospace platforms for precision sensor integration and responsiveness. It performs best in engagements against other small craft and missiles rather than capital-scale targets, and operates effectively in the confined tactical space around a Pocket WarShip or space station. This specialization carries tradeoffs: without numerical support, the Würger cannot sustain prolonged engagements against dedicated assault craft, and its point-defense role leaves it reliant on coordinated wing tactics to compensate for individual firepower limits.

The Würger Assault Craft is a purpose-built small craft developed by Lockheed/CBM on Furillo for the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces, entering service in 3099. It was designed to fill the growing need for dedicated orbital screening platforms in an era when Pocket WarShips had become a fixture of Inner Sphere naval operations. Rather than relying on aerospace fighters to screen capital ships and space stations, the LCAF sought a specialized craft optimized for missile interdiction and close-in defense work. The Würger represents Lockheed/CBM's answer to that requirement, building on earlier small craft concepts to deliver a more capable and electronically integrated platform suited to the demands of Dark Age naval warfare.

The Würger serves as an orbital escort and interdiction platform within the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces, most commonly deployed in wings assigned to Pocket WarShip screens and system defense stations. It performs best in coordinated groups, where numerical advantage over larger assault craft compensates for its individual firepower limits. The type has seen consistent use along the Lyran-Clan border, where the threat of orbital bombardment and deep-space boarding actions has made mobile, responsive small craft a standing priority for LCAF commanders.

The Jihad fundamentally reshaped naval warfare across the Inner Sphere. The prolific use of anti-ship missiles against DropShips and capital ships prompted widespread adoption of robust point-defense systems, seen in vessels like the Interdictor and the Arondight-class DropShips. By 3094, the NL-45 had become the first small craft purpose-built for missile defense and interdiction, establishing a new category of dedicated naval support craft. The Würger followed in 3099 as the next step in that evolution, incorporating the more integrated sensor and control architecture of the Progeny II computer and pushing the concept further toward a true fleet screening platform.

The design's capabilities were demonstrated during the Jade Falcon offensive of 3143. Archon Vedet Brewer had positioned substantial forces to defend Westerstede, including multiple Würger wings operating alongside two Bastion-class and one Battlesat-class system defense stations. When Jade Falcon DropShips arrived, they split into three groups: one to engage the LCAF fighter screen, one to push 'Mech transports toward the planet, and a third of battle taxis held in reserve to board the stations once the screen was cleared.

For four hours the LCAF fighter screen and the Jade Falcons fought to a standstill. Engine damage then forced the LCS Akfata, an Isegrim-class assault DropShip, to withdraw, and the Clan forces saw their opening, burning hard for the defense stations. The waiting Würger wings launched from their bays and engaged the Clan craft during the vulnerable deceleration burn. Outnumbered more than two-to-one, the Jade Falcon assault craft eventually withdrew to their transports. Five battle taxis breached the screen and delivered boarding parties, but all were repelled with minimal casualties among the defenders.

The Würgers then rejoined the wider dogfight, giving the LCAF fighter wing time to return to the stations and rearm. When those fighters came back less than half an hour later, the Clan forces retreated to their jump point. Though the archon ultimately ordered the abandonment of Westerstede in favor of fortifying Tharkad, the Würgers had maintained the LCAF's orbital presence throughout, denying the Jade Falcons air support and reconnaissance for the duration of the planetside campaign.

The Mówáng is a 100-ton Civilian Aerodyne Small Craft powered by a standard fusion powerplant delivering a safe thrust of 4G and a maximum thrust of 6G, providing adequate performance for intra-system transit between planetary surfaces, orbital stations, and jump points. Fuel capacity supports routine system hops without requiring intermediate resupply. The craft's three-man crew is drawn from the employing noble's personal staff, valued for discretion rather than combat experience.

Passenger accommodations are modest but well-appointed for a vessel of this class. A single first-class stateroom serves the primary passenger, while two steerage-rated cabins accommodate aides or companions. Cargo capacity is limited to five and a half tons, accessed through a single cargo door, which is sufficient for personal effects, gifts, or contraband at the owner's discretion.

Armor protection amounts to just two and a half tons of standard plating, arranged to deflect debris rather than withstand weapons fire. The Mówáng carries no armament whatsoever. These limitations reflect deliberate design choices: military protection would raise costs and attract inspection. The craft's entire defensive strategy rests on appearing unremarkable. Its construction is intentionally within the manufacturing capability of any modestly industrialized world, which is reflected in its price tag of roughly 3.5 million C-bills.

The Mówáng-class Courier is a compact civilian Small Craft conceived during the early First Succession War to serve the personal transport needs of Capellan Confederation nobility. Commissioned by the House of Scions in 2835, the design was built around simplicity, passenger comfort, and low production cost. The House declared an open manufacturing license immediately upon introduction, inviting any world with adequate industrial capacity to build the craft without restriction. That decision spread the Mówáng across dozens of systems within a few generations, making it among the most widely distributed personal spacecraft in the Inner Sphere. Lightly built and unarmed, the vessel relies on its mundane appearance and near-universal familiarity to pass scrutiny wherever it operates.

The Clandestine variant operates exclusively as a covert assault transport for Word of Blake operatives during the Jihad period. Outwardly indistinguishable from a standard Mówáng, the craft approaches its objective concealed within the traffic of a civilian DropShip or JumpShip, then separates for its attack run. The Angel ECM suite is activated before approach to jam communications and degrade tracking, followed by bombing of the target site. Two Level Is of battle armor are then deployed for ground operations, and the craft stands by to extract the troops or continue suppressing first responders with additional bomb runs. The Internal Bomb Bay is the primary stand-off weapon, used both before and after troop deployment.

The Mówáng-class Courier emerged in the early years of the First Succession War, when established DropShip service networks grew unreliable and Capellan nobles sought alternatives for private intra-system travel. The House of Scions, the aristocratic body overseeing Capellan nobility, sponsored the design with specific requirements: the craft had to be affordable, simple to build, and comfortable enough for a Diem to use as a personal vehicle. The open manufacturing license declared in 2835 was a deliberate policy choice, intended to maximize production across the Confederation's many worlds rather than concentrate output at a handful of licensed facilities. Within decades, the design had spread throughout the Capellan Confederation and was being produced by local manufacturers on dozens of worlds.

Throughout the Succession Wars the Mówáng occupied a quiet but persistent niche. Capellan Diems used them to travel between worlds in their multi-planetary holdings, convey valuables, and move goods, licit or otherwise, beyond the reach of formal customs networks. Their unremarkable profile meant that military and customs patrols rarely subjected them to serious scrutiny. As the design spread beyond the Confederation, nobles and wealthy merchants in neighboring states acquired them for the same reasons. By the time of the Clan Invasion, the Mówáng had become common enough in Inner Sphere system traffic that a single craft could move through most ports without comment.

That anonymity proved dangerous during the Jihad. In 3073, the Word of Blake acquired a number of Mówáng hulls provided by Kali Liao and modified them as covert assault transports. The conversions stripped out passenger quarters, installed battle armor bays capable of carrying two Level Is of troops, reduced the engine output to free internal volume, increased armor protection to four tons, and fitted an Angel ECM suite. The modified craft were used as clandestine insertion vehicles, exploiting the Mówáng's civilian identity to approach targets aboard passenger DropShips or JumpShips before executing attack runs. Most of these converted hulls were destroyed or captured before the Jihad concluded, but the episode left a residual wariness. Several jurisdictions instituted enhanced inspection requirements for Mówáng-type craft in the early Republic era, and the vessel's reputation as an innocent courier was never fully restored.
